questions.question: When stopping at an intersection, use your mirrors to:

options.text: Check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
Look for dark clouds that may mean bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if drivers behind you see that you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see vehicles approaching from behind. Make sure drivers notice you and respond to your actions when you stop.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Test your brake lights to make sure they work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Test your brake lights to make sure they work.
questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test both brake controls to make sure each one activates the brake lights.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket when it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a strong jacket with long sleeves when riding, even in warm weather.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply controlled pressure to both brakes at the same time to stop quickly. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: The best clothing for a motorcyclist:

options.text: Does not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you in a crash while keeping you comfortable and visible to other drivers.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: Unlike other substances, alcohol:

options.text: Is quickly absorbed into the bloodstream.
Needs to be digested to enter the bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is quickly absorbed into the bloodstream.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested before entering the bloodstream. It is absorbed directly through the stomach and small intestine walls, quickly reaching the brain.

questions.question: You should pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you most visible and gives you safe space around your bike.
You like, without thinking about other drivers.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you most visible and gives you safe space around your bike.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you and where you have space around your motorcycle. Change your position as road conditions change. There is no single best position to always use.

questions.question: Reflective and brightly colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn when riding at night.
Help other drivers see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you on the road.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Places you right next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a position in your lane that helps you avoid hazards. Keep safe space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: When riding, wear boots or shoes that:
questions.explanation: Your shoes should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they don't catch on things. Keep laces tucked in so they don't get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy footwear that is high enough to cover and support your ankles. Soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What colors should motorcycle riders wear?
questions.explanation: Bright orange, red, yellow, and green are the best colors for riders to wear. These colors help other drivers see you.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same place as on your motorcycle.
Take it right out on the highway.
Get used to it in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get used to it in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Learn where all the controls are on a new motorcycle. Practice riding it in a safe area before taking it on the road.

questions.question: Wind noise while riding:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.

questions.explanation: Long-term exposure to wind noise can cause permanent hearing damage. Use ear plugs or hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:
questions.explanation: The safest way to deal with a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Your motorcycle should fit you properly. This means:

options.text: Your fingertips should barely touch the handlebars when seated.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when standing next to it.
Your feet should reach the ground comfortably when seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should reach the ground comfortably when seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you right when your feet can comfortably touch the ground while you are seated. Make sure a motorcycle fits before you ride it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols and tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: When choosing a jacket for protection, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or another sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose pants and a jacket made of leather or sturdy material. They should fit snugly without flapping in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most?
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go slower than 25 mph, such as construction equipment, farm machinery, or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: When selecting a protective jacket, a motorcycle rider should look for one that is:

options.text: Made of leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Wear protective apparel when riding a motorcycle. Choose a jacket that covers your arms completely and fits snugly while letting you move freely. Leather or sturdy synthetic materials with body armor offer the best protection.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection in a crash?
questions.explanation: Sturdy leather or synthetic materials provide the best protection in an accident. Wear long pants and a jacket while riding.
